title: Large space after prompt with fish on arch linux on arm
body:
<!--
─────────────────────────────────────────────
  ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Please run the following command to create an issue:

  starship bug-report

  An issue will be pre-populated with your system's configuration,
  making the process a whole lot quicker 😊
─────────────────────────────────────────────
-->

## Bug Report

#### Current Behavior
A large space appears following the prompt instead of the regular single space.

#### Expected Behavior
A single space after the prompt.

#### Additional context/Screenshots
This problem seems to be *very* specific. It only happens with fish, it only happens when using arch linux (I think - not tested too thoroughly), and it only happens on my raspberry pi 3b. It doesn't seem to be determined by the terminal emulator (I've tried a few on different platforms).

I've also tried building starship from the source *without* lines 82-84 in `print.rs`:
```rs
    // A workaround for a fish bug (see #739,#279). Applying it to all shells
    // breaks things (see #808,#824,#834). Should only be printed in fish.
    if Shell::Fish == context.shell && context.target == Target::Main {
        buf.push_str("\x1b[J"); // An ASCII control code to clear screen
    }
```
.. but that also didn't work.

I've honestly got no idea if this is an issue with starship, fish, or even some weird bug with rust or arch linux on arm, but I figured this was a reasonable starting point.

Here's the issue:
![image](https://github.com/starship/starship/assets/31170809/2aba49e1-a864-41dd-b605-526b706c542d)

And here's the expected behavior:
![image](https://github.com/starship/starship/assets/31170809/68223b3e-f69a-4ed0-bcf8-65bd8b8df20c)

It's even more prevalent with some other configurations (needs more testing):
![image](https://github.com/starship/starship/assets/31170809/2e981d5b-48df-4661-ad0b-fb185159f057)

#### Environment
- Starship version: 1.18.2
- Shell type: fish
- Shell version: 3.7.1
- Terminal emulator: Windows Terminal, conhost, and Termux.
- Operating system:
```
$ uname --all
Linux alarmpi 6.6.25-1-rpi #1 SMP Fri Apr  5 13:33:52 MDT 2024 armv7l GNU/Linux
```

#### Relevant Shell Configuration
Occurs with default fish configuration + `starship init fish | source`

#### Starship Configuration
Occurs with default starship configuration (i.e. no config file).

comments.body:
You sure it does that?
Pls check again. Cuz it used to happen to me but I check the config. Populated it and override it. Do not put space after ```$character```. Idk if this will help but still I think it worked on me so 😞😞😕

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Pretty sure, yep. I've managed to work out that using just
```toml
format = "❱"
```
as the config causes the issue.

![image](https://github.com/starship/starship/assets/31170809/d55890a0-1fe7-4b1a-8651-a62fdba71fa3)

Interestingly, it doesn't seem to happen with other characters. For example, just using `>` works as expected without the extra spaces.

Using more `❱`s in the prompt seems to increase the number of spaces at the end. I'd guess it's an issue to do with how specific characters are handled on certain platforms?

comments.body: Moreover, please check if the remote system is using a UTF-8 locale and that it is present on the system (`/etc/locale.gen`). The value of `$LANG` should contain `UTF-8`.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Might be with font substitution. Are you using kitty terminal?

No, I've tried with several terminals, including Windows Terminal and conhost on windows, and Termux on android.

> Share me your config

The minimal config to replicate it is just ```toml
format = "❱"```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Moreover, please check if the remote system is using a UTF-8 locale and that it is present on the system (`/etc/locale.gen`). The value of `$LANG` should contain `UTF-8`.

It seems like `$LANG` was actually set to `C` instead of `en_US.UTF-8` (which is what I use on other systems where this config works), but unfortunately updating `/etc/locale.conf` and rebooting doesn't seem to fix the issue. Could still be related though?

comments.body: Did you make sure the locale is not commented in `/etc/locale.gen` and did you run `locale-gen`? Maybe also try changing the locale via `localectl`.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Did you make sure the locale is not commented in `/etc/locale.gen` and did you run `locale-gen`? Maybe also try changing the locale via `localectl`.

Oh I really should've double checked a guide on how to change that! I only uncommented the line and didn't run `locale-gen`. It's all working now with the correct locale.

Thanks for your help!

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I am still a bit curious as to why this doesn't happen with other shells (it was fine with bash), but the locale being wrong was definitely the issue.
